A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pfaffian algorithm-configuration work. All 51 pages of v2 and 56 pages of v4, including Appendices A–E, support comparison; retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports theoretical guarantees, proofs, and illustrative functions, including in its appendices. References to empirical success concern cited work, not original experiments.

after.justification: V4 likewise contains theoretical results and illustrations, without original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Lemma 5.6 corrects the stated parameter-selection rule from minimizing to maximizing empirical utility. This is a limited procedural correction; the Pfaffian GJ operations, application algorithms, and Appendix D.2 Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or test scenarios in reported experiments. Clustering, graph-based semi-supervised learning, and logistic regression remain theoretical applications.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. Revisions to comparisons with earlier theoretical frameworks belong to research positioning and theory.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocols appear in either version. V4's added logistic-regression sample-size and parameter restrictions are theoretical assumptions, not changes to conducted evaluations.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, empirical robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or experimental case analyses. The retained piecewise-function illustrations are explanatory examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changes to theoretical probability bounds are assessed under T1.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries, performance rankings, or measured findings to update. The illustrative plots are retained; revisions to symbolic guarantees belong to T1.

T1.justification: V4 corrects Rademacher normalization and H dependence in Section 5.3.1, and revises Theorem 6.5 to distinguish N problem instances from m training samples and state a utility-gap guarantee. It explicitly assumes m' < m and positive regularization bounds, corrects the degree exponent in Lemma B.2, and removes the standard Theorem A.1 and proof. The principal Pfaffian bounds and online proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the Pfaffian GJ framework, refined piecewise guarantees, a dispersion-verification tool, and the same three application areas. Recovery of the earlier logistic-regression guarantee was already acknowledged in v2.

C2.justification: V4 explains the roles of algorithm randomization, smoothed adversaries, full-information feedback, and dispersion in relating online and statistical guarantees. Its conclusion adds limitations concerning lower bounds and computational efficiency. Section 6.2 also removes v2's assertion that the cited graph-labeling algorithms are equivalent.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 retains the same approximation procedures and Algorithms 1–2. No code or data access information, implementation settings, hardware specifications, or runtime disclosures are added.

R1.justification: V4 adds related work on pricing, neural-network hyperparameter tuning, dynamic/internal regret, bandit tuning, and efficient configuration. It refines the linkage comparison and explicitly acknowledges the similarity of its logistic-regression proof to Balcan et al. [2023b]. The central positioning beyond rational-function GJ frameworks remains.

P1.justification: Substantial paragraph rewriting and editing affect the abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and application explanations. V4 adds an accessible computation-tree overview, expands the online-learning narrative, standardizes 'distributional' to 'statistical,' reorganizes Appendix A, and adds substantive future-directions discussion and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V4 adds the introductory framework diagram as Figure 1 and redisplays v2 Figure 1(a) as Figure 2. The original two figures remain as Figures 3–4, with caption and placement adjustments. The single-column layout and algorithm displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The clearer framework overview, explicit online-learning assumptions, and corrections to Rademacher and logistic-regression guarantees improve accessibility and mathematical precision while preserving the central contribution. The gain is limited: v4's conversion to utility h = H - loss leaves an inconsistent minimization definition for the optimal parameter in Section 6.3.1.
